meta.description: Compute and interpret VCF quality-control metrics including Ti/Tv, het/hom, missingness, HWE, contamination signals, and sample relatedness with bcftools, VCFtools, identity tools, and cyvcf2.

scientific_integrity.detail: All reported numerical values were generated from retained synthetic fixtures and cross-checked against command outputs; no literature identifiers, clinical results, or statistics were invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The outputs remained callset and cohort quality-control analyses and made no patient-specific diagnosis or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill correctly requires matched-cohort interpretation, genotype filtering before cohort metrics, ancestry-aware comparisons, controls-only excess-heterozygosity assessment, and identity reconciliation before downstream analysis.

code_usability.detail: The shipped cyvcf2 example and every exercised bcftools and VCFtools workflow ran successfully. Two edge-output presentation gaps remain, but neither makes the code unrunnable or corrupts the corrected multiallelic Ti/Tv and QUAL calculations.

functional_suitability.note: The broad QC workflow is scientifically complete, but the example labels PASS-or-dot records as PASS and omits substitution counts when the transversion denominator is zero.

reliability.note: Empty files, missing QUAL, multiallelic SNPs, prior cohort data, and all broader CLI workflows complete deterministically; two valid edge cases produce incomplete or ambiguous presentation rather than a crash.

performance_context.note: The Skill layers concise operational guidance over a separate usage guide and streams VCF records through mature command-line tools.

agent_usability.note: Decision tables, ordering constraints, command patterns, and common-error remedies are directly actionable; one example label is inconsistent with the documented FILTER distinction.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language, example prompts, a quick reference, and explicit contextual interpretation make the Skill easy to discover and use.

security.note: No credentials, destructive commands, or dynamic code execution are present; the example delegates malformed-path and malformed-VCF validation to cyvcf2.

maintainability.note: The documentation and short example are modular and independently testable, although the summary-printing branch couples count visibility to a nonzero denominator.

agent_specific.note: Trigger scope, progressive disclosure, idempotent read-only workflows, and handoffs to filtering and normalization Skills are strong; the custom script output contract could be more explicit.

assertions.note: The script and bcftools independently reported two transitions and two transversions.

assertions.text: A valid QUAL value of zero contributes to the mean quality.
assertions.note: The script reported 20.0 for observed qualities 0, 20, and 40; dropping zero would have produced 30.0.

assertions.text: The custom summary distinguishes strict PASS records from unfiltered-dot records.
assertions.note: It printed PASS variants: 3, while bcftools found two strict-PASS records and three PASS-or-dot records.

assertions.text: Filtered records remain separate from not-failed records.
assertions.note: One LowQual record was reported as filtered, and bcftools confirmed the 2/3 strict-versus-not-failed split.

key_strengths: The corrected cyvcf2 example counts every alternate SNP allele and preserves valid QUAL zero values, with independent bcftools agreement.
The Skill gives methodologically sound, context-dependent guidance for Ti/Tv, missingness, HWE, contamination signals, and ancestry-aware cohort interpretation.
The documented biallelic allele-balance matcher retains phased and unphased 0/1 and 1/0 orientations while explicitly routing multiallelic AD to a real parser.
The broader bcftools and VCFtools workflows executed successfully for cohort statistics, exact HWE, callset comparison, stratification, identity checking, and relatedness.

recommendations.title: Separate strict PASS from unfiltered records
recommendations.problem: The example increments pass whenever cyvcf2 exposes FILTER as null, which includes both strict PASS and the unfiltered dot state, then prints the combined count as PASS variants.
recommendations.root_cause: The output contract uses one counter for two VCF FILTER states even though the Skill documentation correctly distinguishes them.
recommendations.fix: Report strict PASS and unfiltered-dot records as separate counters, or rename the current count to Not-failed variants (PASS or dot) and add a strict-PASS counter using an API-safe distinction. Add a three-record PASS/dot/LowQual regression.

recommendations.title: Report Ti/Tv components when denominator is zero
recommendations.problem: When a valid callset has transitions but zero transversions, the example suppresses both component counts because the entire print block is guarded by transversions greater than zero.
recommendations.root_cause: Presentation of the counts is coupled to whether the ratio has a nonzero denominator.
recommendations.fix: Always print transition and transversion counts. Print Ti/Tv as infinite or undefined with an explicit zero-denominator note when transversions are zero, and add transition-only and empty-VCF regressions.
